description: Racket extraction-fidelity corpus. Ground truth is Racket's own expander (see oracle.rkt), so every target must be a module the local Racket install can expand AND instantiate.

pinning.policy: The collects tree is pinned by the Racket VERSION rather than a git SHA -- it ships with the toolchain, so the interpreter identifies the corpus. results.json records the version it was measured against; a run under a different Racket is measuring a different corpus.
pinning.instantiation: oracle.rkt calls dynamic-require to test whether an export is a procedure, which RUNS module top-level code. Targets must be libraries, never scripts with side effects.

targets.stresses: Heavy macrology, contract wrappers, re-export shims. racket/list.rkt alone defines twelve names via (define-lgetter second 2) -- real, exported, human-written names no static parser can see.
Bootstrapping code and the class system internals: define/public, mixins, deep syntax-case.
